The grassy place where I hunt is the edge of the wood, where the meadow begins. It is soft underfoot, and the wind moves through it like a whisper. I sit on a branch and watch, listening for the rustle of voles or the flicker of a mouse. The grass is tall in places, and I must be careful not to trip. I sit still and listen, and when I hear a mouse, I strike. The grass is good for hiding, and the earth is good for pouncing. I know the place well, and I know where the mice go. It is a good place to hunt.

The grassy place where I hunt is the meadow by the stream. It moves with the wind, and the grasses are tall and thick. I sit on a branch high above it, and when I see a mouse or a vole, I drop. Mice. The ones that come out in the dark and scuttle through the grass. I hear them under the leaves, and I pounce. They are the most common. I also eat voles, shrews, and sometimes slugs. But mice are the main one. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Voles. I can hear them in the leaf litter under the hawthorn. Their breathing is like a low hum, and their movements are like a whisper. I can hear them even when they are not moving. I catch them with a quick dive and a twist of my neck. They are soft and warm, and they fill my belly.

Voles. They make up most of my diet. I hear them under the leaves and the leaves give way when I strike. I kill them with my beak and swallow them whole. I do not like the sound of them. They squeak like a rat. I also eat earthworms, mice, and sometimes a frog. But voles are the most common. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Voles. The brown ones. I eat them by the dozen in the autumn. I can hear them in the soil under the leaves, and I strike down through the leaves, sometimes through the snow, and take them out by the neck.
Voles. I sit on the branch and listen for the scratch-scratch-scratch of a voles' burrow. I strike down and take the one that comes out.

Mice. I can hear their scratching under the leaves. I can smell them in the soil. I can see them at the edge of the wood. I strike and kill them with my beak. They are the most common. I eat them whole, bones and all. I have no use for them. They are food. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Mice. Most of them. I hear them under the leaves, under the bark, under the soil. I strike and kill them with my beak. I tear them apart and eat them. I do not like them, but I need them. They are the most common. I also eat voles, and sometimes a field mouse or a shrew. But mice are the most. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Mice. I eat a mouse every two or three days, and I can tell when I have had one. They are soft, and they smell like the earth. I kill them with my beak, then swallow them whole. I do not chew. The rest of the time I sit still and wait.

Voles. Most of my diet is voles. They are small, fat, and easy to catch in the meadow. I listen for their squeaks and rustles under the leaves. I pounce, and they are mine. Sometimes I catch a mouse or a beetle, but voles are the main thing. I eat them whole, bones and all. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Mice. Most of them. I hear them in the wood, and I fly down and catch them. Sometimes voles, sometimes shrews, but mice are the most common. I eat them whole, head first, and I swallow the bones. I remember when I was young, I didn't know that. I thought I was eating just the meat. But the bones go down too. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Voles. They are the most common. They are small and dark and soft and smell like earth. I catch them in the leaf litter, sometimes under a stone. I eat them whole, but I chew the bones. I remember the taste of them. They are good.

Voles. I eat voles. Most of them. The rest is beetles, caterpillars, earthworms, mice, and sometimes a small bird or a frog. I eat them whole, head first. I can hear them under the leaves, and I strike. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.
Voles. I eat them by the hundred in the autumn. They are soft and fat and they come out in the dark. I sit still and wait.

Voles. I can hear them under the leaves in the meadow, and I can hear their breathing. They are the most common sound in the dark. I can hear them under the bark of the old oak, and I can hear them in the stream. I catch them with my feet, and then I kill them with my beak.
Voles. The meadow is a maze of burrows and tunnels. I sit on a branch and wait. When I hear a volesnudge, I drop.

I eat mostly voles. They are small, and there are many of them. I hear them in the meadow, and I can tell by the sound how many are there. I catch them with my feet, and then I kill them with my beak. Sometimes I eat mice too, and sometimes I find a field mouse in the hedgerow. But voles are the most common. I can eat a whole one in one go. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo

I prefer voles. They are small, quick, and plentiful. I can hear them moving under the leaves, and I can strike fast. Sometimes I catch a mouse, but they are harder to find. The shrews are too small, and the rats are too big. Voles are the best. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

My favourite prey is the voles. They are plentiful, easy to catch, and they run in the undergrowth where I can hear them. I can hear them under the leaves, and I strike down through the brambles. Their squeaks are like the sound of a small animal in distress, and I love the way they twitch and run. I catch them with my feet, and they make a soft, wet sound when I eat them. I prefer voles. They are common, and I can hear them moving under the leaves. Their squeaks are easy to track. But I also eat mice, shrews, and sometimes slugs. The bigger the prey, the more I need to work for it. I don’t like worms—they’re too slimy and hard to swallow. Hare is good, but rare. I wait for the right moment.

My favourite prey is voles. They are plentiful, easy to catch, and their squeaks are like little bells in the dark. I can hear them under the leaves and in the soil, and I strike fast. Sometimes I catch a shrew or a mouse, but voles are the best. I eat them whole, head first, and the rest goes down. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

My favourite prey is a vole. They are small, quick, and plentiful. I can hear them under the leaves and soil, and I can strike fast. They taste good too, though I don't think about that. I just know they fill me up. Sometimes I catch a shrew or a mouse, but voles are the best. They come out at dusk, and I sit still and wait. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

My favourite prey is voles. They are common, they are fat, and they are always under the leaves. I can hear them moving through the soil, and I can smell them when they are near. I wait for them to come up, and then I pounce. Voles are easy. But I also like mice, and sometimes I catch a shrew. I don't like earthworms—they are too slimy and I can't see them well. Hoo... hoo

My favourite prey is voles. They are small, quick, and plentiful. I can hear them under the leaves, and the sound is like a mouse under a stone. I sit still, wait, and strike. Voles are the best. Sometimes I get a shrew or a mouse, but voles are the best. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I do not have a favourite. Voles are most common, but I eat what I can find. A field vole is good, fat, and quick. A shrew is small but sharp. A mouse is like a vole, but smaller. I eat them all when I can. The best is when I find a fat one in the moonlight. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

My favourite prey is a vole. They are common, they are fat, and they are easy to catch. I hear them under the leaves, and I drop down from the branch. They don’t see me, and I grab them with my feet. Sometimes I eat them whole, sometimes I tear them apart. They are good.

My favourite prey is the voles. They are small, fast, and plentiful. I can hear them moving under the leaves, and their squeaks are unmistakable. I sit still, wait, and strike. Voles are the most reliable food in the wood. I also eat mice, shrews, and sometimes a young rabbit if I’m lucky. But voles... they are my staple. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I prefer voles. They are small, quick, and always under the leaves. I can hear them moving through the soil, and I wait until they come up to breathe. Then I pounce. Voles are the most common, and they fill my belly. But I also eat mice, shrews, and even slugs when I'm hungry. The meadow is full of food. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I do not have a favourite. Voles are the most common, and they are always there. But I also eat mice, shrews, beetles, and sometimes even a young field mouse. The shrews are tricky—they run fast and have a bad smell. I prefer the voles. They are easy to catch, and they are always under the leaves. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I prefer voles. They are small, fat, and quick. I can hear them moving under the leaves, and when I drop, they don't see me. Sometimes I catch a mouse too, but voles are better. They fill my belly. I eat them in the dark, when the moon is full and the grass is still. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

The voles. They are small, quick, and plentiful. I can hear them under the leaves, and I can strike fast. Sometimes I catch them in the grass, sometimes I dive from the branch. They taste good, too. I do not like the mice—they are too small and often too many. And the shrews... I avoid them. They are bad news. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

My favourite prey is a vole. They are fat, they run in the leaf litter, and I can hear them under the soil. I wait in the hollow and strike. They are quick, but I am faster. I eat them whole, bones and all.
The voles. Small, quick, and plenty. They run through the grass under the moon. I sit still and wait.

Hares, voles, mice, shrews, beetles and the odd frog. I see them in the grass with my eyes, and I hear them with my ears. The long grass is thick and soft, but I can still move through it. I hunt voles and mice in the long grass. They are small and quick, but I can hear them through the grass. I sit still and wait, then pounce. Sometimes I catch a shrew or a mole. The grass is soft and hides them well, but I know where to listen. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I do not like the long grass. It is too soft and hides too well. I prefer the hedgerows and the wood. But when the moon is full and the voles are active, I might hunt in the grass near the stream. I can hear them rustling under the leaves. I sit still and wait. The grass is not as good as the leaves for hearing. I prefer the quiet. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

The long grass is a place to hide, not to hunt. I hunt in the meadow, the streamside, the wood. The grass is too thick and soft for my feet. I sit still and wait. The voles come out. I hear them under the leaves. I strike.
I hunt voles and shrews in the long grass. They come out at dusk and run through the meadow. I sit still and wait, then drop from the bramble. I can hear them under the soil. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I hunt voles and mice in the long grass. They rustle under the leaves and I can hear them. I fly down and strike. The grass is thick, but I can see the movement. I use my feet to feel for them too. Sometimes I catch a shrew or a mole. I don't like the long grass much—it's too hot and the prey is hard to find. I prefer the wood. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I do not hunt in the long grass. The long grass is the meadow, and there I hunt voles and mice. The grass is too tall for me to see well, and the voles stay close to the ground. I prefer the hedgerows and the wood. The long grass is too soft and the voles are too quick. I sit still and wait for the rustle. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I do not hunt in the long grass. I hunt in the wood, in the hedgerows, in the meadow. The long grass is too soft, too warm, and too full of insects. I prefer the cold, the silence, the dark. I hunt the voles, the mice, the shrews, the moles. I hunt the field-mouse, the earthworm, the beetles. I do not hunt in the long grass. I am not a bird

I do not like the long grass. It is too thick and hides too well. I prefer the open meadow and the wood. In the meadow, I hunt voles and mice. They come out in the evening, and I can hear them under the leaves. In the wood, I catch shrews and sometimes a young mouse. The long grass is dangerous. I have seen a fox there once. It was not good. I stay clear of the long grass. Hoo...

I do not hunt in the long grass. The long grass is where the voles are. I sit in the oak and wait for the vole to come out. I hear the rustle of the grass and the crunch of the soil. The grass hides them well, but I can smell them. I have to be careful not to tip the grass too much, or they'll run. I wait for the right moment, then strike.

Hares, voles, mice, shrews, earthworms, beetles, slugs and the odd frog. I hunt in the long grass with the same care as I do in the undergrowth. I listen, I wait, I strike. I hunt voles. They come up from the meadow in the long grass. I sit on the fence, or on the edge of the wood, and wait. When I hear them, I fly down and strike. They are quick, but I am quicker. I eat them whole, bones and all.
Hedgehogs, voles, mice, shrews, beetles, worms and caterpillars. I go in with a soft, low flight and a loud call. The grass is soft and I can hear the twitch of a hedgehog.

I hunt voles. They run in the long grass near the stream, and I hear them under the leaves. I sit still, wait, and then pounce. The grass is soft and makes noise, so I have to be careful not to trip. Sometimes I catch a shrew, but voles are better. I can hear them from far away, even when they're underground. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I swallow whole the mice I catch. I don't chew them. I just crunch them in my beak and swallow them whole. It's quick and efficient. I don't swallow the acorns, though. I crack them open and eat the seeds. But the mice... they go in whole. I can feel them in my throat, all squishy and warm. I swallow whole what I can. Small prey, like voles or shrews, I eat whole. I don't chew. I just swallow them. But if something is too big, I can't. I'll leave it. I remember once I tried to swallow a large mouse and it got stuck. I had to cough it up. That was messy. So I learned to be careful. I only take what I can handle. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I swallow whole the whole of a vole, the whole of a mouse, the whole of a shrew. I swallow whole the whole of a night. I swallow whole the whole of the world when I am hunting. I swallow whole the whole of my hunger. I swallow whole the whole of the dark. I swallow whole the whole of my life.

I swallow whole what I catch in my beak. Small prey like voles, shrews, and mice. I can't chew, so I just swallow them whole. Sometimes I catch a frog or a beetle, but those are smaller. I remember the taste of a shrew—bitter and sharp. I never eat anything I can't swallow whole. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

Swallow whole? I swallow whole voles, mice, shrews, slugs, beetles, earthworms, and even the occasional frog. I don't chew. I just open my beak wide and let it go. I swallow whole the mice I catch. I don't chew them, just swallow them whole. The fur goes through, and the bones and teeth stay in my stomach. I can feel them, and sometimes I'll regurgitate them if they're too big. It's a way to get rid of the hard parts. I also swallow whole the seeds I find in the hedgerows, but I don't digest them. I can tell when I've swallowed something big because my belly feels full and heavy. Sometimes I cough it up if it's too big. But mostly, I keep it inside. That's how I survive the winter.

Mice. They are small, quick and tasty. I catch them in the meadow by the stream, under the bark of old oaks. I hear them scurrying, then drop from the branch above. They squeak when I grab them. I eat them whole, bones and all.

I catch voles most. They are small and quick, but I hear them under the leaves and strike fast. I also catch mice, shrews, and sometimes a field vole. The voles are the most common. I hear them in the meadow, and I wait for the right moment. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I catch voles most. They are small, quick, and plentiful. I hear them under the leaves, and when they move, I drop from the branch. They are soft and make a good meal. Sometimes I get a mouse too, but voles are more common. I don't like shrews—they smell bad and are too small for a proper meal. I prefer something that fills my belly and leaves me satisfied.

I catch voles most. They are small and quick, but I can hear them under the leaves. I sit still and wait for the rustle. When I hear it, I drop and grab them with my feet. They squeak and kick, but I hold tight. Sometimes I get a mouse too, but voles are more common. I eat them whole, bones and all. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

The voles. They are small, quick, and plentiful. I hear them scurrying through the undergrowth, and I drop from the branch. Their squeaks are like the sound of a mouse under a stone. I catch them with my beak, and they taste like earth and roots. I eat them whole, bones and all. I don't care for the mice. They are too loud and too far away. I prefer the voles. Hoo... hoo-hoo

I catch voles most. They are small, quick, and often come out at dusk. I listen for their scurrying in the undergrowth, and when I hear the rustle, I drop from the branch. They are good to eat, and there are many of them in the meadow. I also catch mice, shrews, and even a few field mice when they are bold. But voles are the most common. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

A mouse. They are small, quick and numerous. I catch them in the meadow, under the hawthorn, in the old yew. I hear them rustling in the dry leaves, and I drop from the branch above. Sometimes I miss, but more often I strike and they are gone.

Mice. I catch them in the dry grass and under the bracken. They are small and quick, but I can hear them moving through the leaves. I sit still and wait, then pounce. I don't need to chase them far. They are the easiest to catch.
Mice. Small, brown, squeaky. I catch them in the dusk, when the light is just right. They run through the leaves and I pounce. I can hear them under the moss. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

The vole. They are small, quick, and under the leaves. I sit still and wait. I hear them in the dry leaves and the moss. I strike. I catch. I eat. They are the most common. The field vole, the meadow vole, the bank vole. I don't care which. They are all the same. I eat them whole. The rest I leave.

I catch voles most. They are small and quick, but I hear them under the leaves and in the soil. I sit still and wait, then strike. They are the most common, and I can eat several in a night. I also catch mice and shrews, but voles are the most frequent. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

I catch voles most. They are small, quick, and under the leaves. I hear them in the meadow, and when I fly down, I can hear them moving. They squeak like a mouse, but they are more plump. I sometimes catch a shrew, but they are too small and too fast. The voles are better, they fill me up. I eat them in the dark, with the moon low. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.
The vole. They are small, quick, and under the leaves. I sit still and wait. They are the most common in the wood.

I catch voles most. They are small and quick, but I hear them under the leaves and the soil. I sit still and wait. They are the most common in the wood. I also catch mice and shrews, but voles are the most. I can hear them in the dark. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

The voles. They are small, quick and under the leaves. I catch them in the dark, with a twitch of the head and a snap. I can hear them better than I can see them. They run in the soil, and I wait until they come up. Then I strike. I eat them whole, skin and all.

I catch voles most. They are small, quick, and often under the leaves. I hear them in the soil, then pounce. They are good to eat, and there are many of them in the meadow. I also catch mice and shrews, but voles are the most common. I don't like the ones in the hedgerow — they are too skittish. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

My home is the hollow in the old ash. I made it. I live in it. It is round and deep, and the bark is soft and warm. I can turn my head in it, and I can sleep with my eyes open. The wind comes through the leaves, and sometimes it smells like rain. I have a mate, and we share the hollow. She is always there. She is my partner, and we raise our young. That is my home. My home is the hollow in the old oak. It's dry, and the wind comes through the leaves. I sleep in the hollow, and I keep the eggs and young there. The hollow is my safe place. I can hear the stream from there, and the meadow is below. I call to my mate from the hollow, and she answers. The hollow is my home, and I am safe there.

My home is the hollow in the old ash by the stream. It's dry and warm, and the kids are safe inside. I sleep in it when the wind is bad, but I prefer the branches above. I can see the whole meadow from there, and the wood, and the stream. It's a good place to watch for prey and keep my mate safe. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

My home is the hollow in the old ash tree. It is dry and warm, and the leaves keep out the wind. I sleep there, and so do my mate and the young. The hollow is safe, and I can hear the stream from it. I do not like the cold, but the hollow keeps me warm.

It is a hollow in the old ash tree by the stream. I made it. It is dry and deep and warm, and it smells of moss and old feathers. I have a nest inside, and I keep it clean. The stream runs past it, and I can hear the water even when I am not there. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.

My home is the hollow in the old ash tree. It is dark and dry, and the bark is rough. I sleep in it at night, and I keep it warm with my wings. The leaves fall in autumn, and I have to be careful not to get too cold. I have a mate who lives nearby, and we share the hollow. She is called Yew. My home is the hollow in the old oak. I have a mate, and we nest in the hollow. We have a brood of young. I sit on the nest at night, and the young call to me. I do not like the rain, but I have a dry spot in the hollow. I keep the hollow warm with my wings. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.
It is a hollow in the old ash tree by the stream. I sleep in it, and so does my mate. We have a brood of young in the spring.

My home is the hollow in the old ash tree. It is dark and warm, and I sit in it all night. I have a mate, and we share it. She is called Hare. I can hear her call from a mile away. The hollow is safe, and the tree is strong. I have raised two young ones there, and I will raise more. It is my home, and I will not leave it. Hoo... hoo-hoo-hooo.
